FN-DK7YTHT-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 236
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Representative Neil Rafferty
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 03/04/2024
House Bill 236 as introduced would reduce sales tax receipts to the Education Trust Fund by an
estimated $10.3 million in Fiscal Year 2025 and $11.2 million annually, beginning in Fiscal
Year 2026 and each year thereafter, by exempting the gross proceeds of the sale of certain baby
supplies, baby formula, maternity clothing, and menstrual hygiene products from state sales and
use tax.
Page 1

FN-DK7YTHT-2
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 236
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Representative Neil Rafferty
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 03/06/2024
House Bill 236 as reported by the Committee on Ways and Means Education would reduce
sales tax receipts to the Education Trust Fund by an estimated $10.3 million in Fiscal Year 2025
and $11.2 million annually, beginning in Fiscal Year 2026 and each year thereafter, by
exempting the gross proceeds of the sale of certain baby supplies, baby formula, maternity
clothing, and menstrual hygiene products from state sales and use tax.
This bill could also decrease sales tax receipts to local governments by a cumulative maximum
of $15.2 million annually, if all local governments adopted the exemption provided by this bill.

House Bill 236 as reported by the Committee on Finance and Taxation Education would reduce
